---
title: "Tutorial: the one-dimensional test"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.align = "center", fig.width = 5, fig.height = 4)
```

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(selectiveHotelling)
```

`selective_truncated_F()` computes a second selective $p$-value, $p_{\mathrm{polar,1d}}$. It
holds fixed everything about the tested observations except one angle, the one that
determines Hotelling's $T^2$. Its reference distribution is then a truncated
$F$ distribution in one dimension, which makes it faster to compute. The price is power:
fixing more of the data leaves less room to detect a difference ([the technical details](technical_details.html)).

```{r onedim-data}
set.seed(123)
X <- rbind(matrix(rnorm(100), ncol = 2), matrix(rnorm(100), ncol = 2) + 3,
           matrix(rnorm(100), ncol = 2) - 3)
init <- c(1, 51, 101)
cl_fun <- function(x) kmeans_with_fixed_init(x, init_centers_idx = init)$cluster
cl <- cl_fun(X)
```

## Any clustering algorithm

With `clustering = "custom"`, the test takes the same clustering function as
`selective_hotelling_bc()` and computes the $p$-value by a Monte Carlo path in one
dimension:

```{r onedim-bc}
res1d <- selective_truncated_F(X, 1, 2, clustering = "custom", method = "bc",
                               cl_fun = cl_fun, cl_obs = cl, M = 1000)
c(onedim = res1d$pval, classical_F = res1d$p_uncond)
```

`p_uncond` is the classical $F$ $p$-value, which ignores the clustering.

## A closed form for k-means

For $k$-means, the $p$-value can be computed exactly, without Monte Carlo, if we also
condition on the whole sequence of assignments made by Lloyd's algorithm:

```{r onedim-exact}
res_exact <- selective_truncated_F(X, 1, 2, clustering = "kmeans", method = "exact",
                                   K = 3, init_centers_idx = init)
res_exact$pval
```

This version conditions on the most, and it is the least powerful of the three tests.

## Which test to use

| Test | Function | Conditions on | Speed | Power |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $p_{\mathrm{polar}}$ | `selective_hotelling_test()`, `selective_hotelling_bc()` | the clustering | slowest | highest |
| $p_{\mathrm{polar,1d}}$ | `selective_truncated_F(method = "bc")` | the clustering and all but one angle | faster | lower |
| $p_{\mathrm{polar,1d}}^{\mathrm{traj}}$ | `selective_truncated_F(method = "exact")` | also the k-means trajectory | instant | lowest |

All three control the selective Type I error. We recommend $p_{\mathrm{polar}}$ unless
computing time is a constraint.
